# A response lost after the server committed the operation. The proxy at
# $PROXY forwards each request to the server; drop-response discards the
# server's reply and closes the client connection.
# Go contract: cli.go:181-188 (print the request ID before sending and name it
# in the error), control.go:122-145 (a known request ID returns its job),
# control.go:208-219 (cancellation is idempotent intent).
server start
taskfile success.json success
taskfile hold.json hold

drop-response /skygo.v1.ControlService/SubmitJob
! skygo --endpoint $PROXY run -f success.json --request-id lost --wait
stderr '^request-id: lost\n'
stderr 'submit \(retry with --request-id lost\): '
! stderr '^job: '
! stdout .

# The job was accepted anyway. Retrying the printed ID returns it rather than
# creating a second job.
skygo --json --endpoint $PROXY run -f success.json --request-id lost --wait
stdout '"state": *"JOB_STATE_SUCCEEDED"'
job-id LOST
skygo jobs list
stdout '^ID +TARGET +STATE\n'$LOST' +local +succeeded\n$'

# A lost cancellation reply still cancels; repeating it is safe.
skygo --json run -f hold.json --request-id hold
job-id HOLD
await-file ready
drop-response /skygo.v1.ControlService/CancelJob
! skygo --endpoint $PROXY jobs cancel $HOLD --yes
! stdout .
! skygo --json run -f hold.json --request-id hold --wait
stdout '"state": *"JOB_STATE_CANCELED"'
stdout '"cancel_requested": *true'
skygo --json --endpoint $PROXY jobs cancel $HOLD --yes
stdout '"id": *"'$HOLD'"'
stdout '"state": *"JOB_STATE_CANCELED"'

server stop
! stderr .
